LESSON: NICODEMUS’ ENCOUNTER WITH JESUS CHRIST

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Life and Ministry of Jesus Christ
Topic 3.4: Nicodemus’ Encounter with Jesus Christ
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Nicodemus’ Encounter with Jesus Christ, part of The Life and Ministry of Jesus Christ in Grade 9 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: how they apply it in their lives. How did Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ change his life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Nicodemus’ Encounter with Jesus Christ in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. relate the significance of the bronze serpent to the mission of Jesus Christ,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Nicodemus’ Encounter with Jesus Christ in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. deduce lessons learnt from John 3:5-7 and its relevance in the life of a Christian,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Nicodemus’ Encounter with Jesus Christ in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. apply lessons learnt in daily life.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Nicodemus’ Encounter with Jesus Christ in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read John 3:1-16 and make summary notes on Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ,
2. team up to role-play the story of Nicodemus’,
3. watch a video on Nicodemus’ conversion,
4. sing a song on Nicodemus’ conversion,
5. read Numbers 21:4-8 and John 3:14-15 and brainstorm on

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Nicodemus’ Encounter with Jesus Christ together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: the skill of teamwork is enhanced as learners contribute in group discussions by sharing

knowledge, resources, and outline the course of action in performing tasks.

• Imagination and Creativity: the skill of making connections is demonstrated as learners take on different roles to complete

assigned tasks.

• Learning to Learn: the skill of reflection on own work is demonstrated as learners write a reflection journal on how they

apply concepts learnt in their lives.

• Self-efficacy: the skill of self-awareness and planning to accomplish tasks is exhibited as learners read John 3:16 and write a

reflection journal on how they will apply it in their lives.

Values:
• Unity: learners take turns in conversations and activities and respect the opinion of others.

• Responsibility: learners engage in assigned roles, tasks, and duties and complete them on time.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Self-awareness: is exhibited as learners communicate their ideas and make decisions on how to manage their lives as guided

by the Holy Bible.

• Problem-solving: is portrayed as learners reflect on their own learning and come up with solutions to the challenges they

face.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. describe Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ,
2. relate the significance of the bronze serpent to the mission of Jesus Christ,
3. deduce lessons learnt from John 3:5-7 and its relevance in the life of a Christian,
4. apply lessons learnt in daily life.

Remember the key question: how they apply it in their lives. How did Nicodemus’ encounter with Jesus Christ change his life?
